document.title: Musharraf: We Are With You in Your Action Plan in Afghanistan (Islamabad 05087)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Secret/Noforn] Ambassador Wendy Chamberlin bluntly tells Musharraf that 9/11 changed the fundamentals of the Afghanistan-Pakistan debate, that there is no inclination to dialogue with the Taliban, and that the Taliban are harboring the terrorists responsible. A less-redacted version of a document previously posted in 2010.

mentions.quote: PRESIDENT MUSHARRAF TOLD THE AMBASSADOR THAT PAKISTAN WAS "WITH YOU IN AN ACTION PLAN FOR AFGHANISTAN."
"WE ARE WITH YOU IN YOUR ACTION PLAN IN AFGHANISTAN."

persons.name: Wendy Chamberlin
persons.role: U.S. Ambassador to Pakistan (presented credentials 13 Sep 2001)

mentions.quote: AMBASSADOR PRESENTED HER CREDENTIALS JUST BEFORE NOON ON THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 13.
FOREIGN SECRETARY INAM UL HAQUE, MILITARY SECRETARY TO THE PRESIDENT BRIG. NADEEM TAJ

persons.name: Nadeem Taj
persons.role: Military Secretary to the President of Pakistan (Brigadier)

mentions.quote: MILITARY SECRETARY TO THE PRESIDENT BRIG. NADEEM TAJ, AND DCM (NOTETAKER) ALSO ATTENDED.
THE MEETING BETWEEN DEPUTY SECRETARY ARMITAGE AND ISID GEN. MAHMUD THE DAY BEFORE
GEN. MAHMUD WOULD HAVE A SERIES OF MEETINGS TODAY, INCLUDING ANOTHER SESSION WITH THE DEPUTY SECRETARY
THE MEETING BETWEEN DEPUTY SECRETARY ARMITAGE AND ISID GEN. MAHMUD THE DAY BEFORE

events.description: Terrorist attacks on New York and Washington.
Armitage met ISI chief Gen. Mahmud in Washington.
Chamberlin presented credentials, then met Musharraf for 40 minutes; Musharraf pledged support for US action plan in Afghanistan.
Second session between Armitage and Gen. Mahmud planned at noon Washington time.
Terrorist attacks in New York and Washington attributed to UBL and al-Qaida.
Deputy Secretary Armitage met ISI chief Gen. Mahmud.
Musharraf issued a second, stronger public statement on the 9/11 attacks the night before.
Ambassador Chamberlin presented credentials, then held a private meeting with Musharraf, Haque, and Taj; Musharraf pledged support for the U.S. action plan in Afghanistan.
Second Armitage–Gen. Mahmud session planned at noon Washington time (2100 Islamabad).
Embassy requested the Secretary of State telephone Musharraf to reinforce Pakistan's commitment to logistical support.

key_claims: Musharraf pledged Pakistan would cooperate with the US against the 9/11 perpetrators and those who supported them.
The US Ambassador told Musharraf that the time for dialogue with the Taliban was over.
Washington suspected Pakistan was sympathetic to the Taliban and bin Ladin; Musharraf denied this.
The US believed the Taliban harbored the 9/11 perpetrators, identified as UBL and al-Qa'ida.
Musharraf wanted UN backing and detailed US requirements to make logistical cooperation politically 'sellable' in Pakistan.
The Embassy recommended that the Secretary of State phone Musharraf to reinforce Pakistan's commitment to logistical support.
